empty-vs-null.name: Empty vs Non-empty Host
empty-vs-null.description: One parser rejects the URL and returns empty/null host while the other extracts a host value

ipv6-case.name: IPv6 Case Normalization
ipv6-case.description: IPv6 hex digits are returned in different cases (upper vs lower) by different parsers

fullwidth-chars.name: Fullwidth Character Normalization
fullwidth-chars.description: Fullwidth Unicode characters (e.g. fullwidth period ．U+FF0E) are normalized to ASCII equivalents by some parsers but not others

ip-normalization.name: IP Address Normalization
ip-normalization.description: Hex, octal, dotless, or otherwise non-standard IP representations are expanded to standard dotted-decimal by some parsers but not others

leading-zeros-ip.name: Leading Zeros in IP Octets
leading-zeros-ip.description: Leading zeros in IPv4 octets are treated as octal by some parsers and rejected or normalized differently by others

percent-encoding.name: Percent-Encoding in Host
percent-encoding.description: Host is returned with percent-encoded sequences by one parser but decoded (or re-encoded) by another

scheme-as-host.name: Scheme Parsed as Host
scheme-as-host.description: Double-scheme URLs (e.g. http://https://...) cause one parser to return the inner scheme as the host value

case-folding.name: Host Case Folding
case-folding.description: Host is lowercased by one parser but returned in original mixed/upper case by another

punycode.name: Punycode / IDN Encoding
punycode.description: Internationalized domain names are encoded to punycode (xn--) by one parser but left as Unicode by another

trailing-dot.name: Trailing Dot in Host
trailing-dot.description: A trailing dot on the hostname is retained by one parser but stripped by another

port-in-host.name: Port Number in Host Field
port-in-host.description: The port number is included in the host field by one parser instead of being separated into a dedicated port field.

userinfo-in-host.name: Userinfo Bleeding into Host
userinfo-in-host.description: The userinfo (username/password) portion bleeds into the host field because the @ sign is not parsed as a userinfo/host delimiter.

ipv6-brackets.name: IPv6 Bracket Handling
ipv6-brackets.description: IPv6 addresses are returned with surrounding brackets by one parser but without brackets (or with partial brackets) by another.

path-affects-host.name: Path Segments Affecting Host Extraction
path-affects-host.description: Dot-segments (/../, /./), single-slash URLs, or other path-like constructs in the authority cause different parsers to extract different host values or fail to parse the host entirely.

unicode-normalization.name: Unicode Normalization (NFC/NFD/NFKC)
unicode-normalization.description: Unicode normalization forms (NFC, NFD, NFKC, NFKD) are applied differently: one parser decomposes or composes Unicode characters (e.g. precomposed vs decomposed Greek letters, circled numbers decoded to ASCII digits) while another returns the raw code points.

ipv6-compression.name: IPv6 Zero-Group Compression
ipv6-compression.description: One parser elides consecutive all-zero groups in an IPv6 address using '::' (zero compression / RFC 5952), while another retains the explicit zeros, resulting in different host strings for the same address.

whitespace-control.name: Whitespace and Control Characters in Host
whitespace-control.description: Whitespace or control characters (tabs, newlines, null bytes) embedded in the host are stripped, replaced, or cause the parser to terminate host extraction at different positions, yielding different host values.

backslash-normalization.name: Backslash Normalization
backslash-normalization.description: WHATWG-compliant parsers treat \ as / in authority; non-compliant parsers leave it literal, extracting a different or empty host.
